scope: 12 high-risk ADR-pair spot-checks named in the 2026-05-18 audit directive; ADR-vs-µservice-implementation reality checks. NOT a 193² exhaustive cross product (that would be noise per audit prompt § ADR coherence).

verdict_codes.ALIGNED: Both ADRs make consistent claims; no implementation drift found
verdict_codes.CONTRADICTS: ADRs disagree OR a µservice implements one ADR's decision in a way that violates another
verdict_codes.RESOLVED_BY_INLINE_FIX: Drift existed; fixed in this delta
verdict_codes.ORPHAN_CITATION: ADR referenced in another artifact but the ADR file does not exist
verdict_codes.QUEUED_FOR_STRUCTURAL_MIGRATION: Drift exists at structural-token level; tracked in registry/placeholder-debt/audit-followups.yaml; not a doctrinal contradiction

pairs.potential_contradiction: Does the api-gateway re-introduce mediator semantics for east-west traffic?
pairs.check: Read ADR-0157 §Decision: API gateway is north-south ONLY (per ADR-0182). East-west uses Cilium L3/L4 + Istio Ambient L7 per ADR-0148 + ADR-0145 Invariants 1+2+3 + direct mTLS gRPC. ADR-0182 explicitly disambiguates.
pairs.rationale: ADR-0182 was authored in PR-143 specifically to disambiguate north-south vs east-west; ADR-0157 (api-gateway tier) carries 'architectural_authority: ADR-0182' in its frontmatter (per pr-143-layered-architecture-audit-report.json cross_ref_updates section)

pairs.lhs: ADR-0148 (Cilium L3/L4 + Istio Ambient L7 layered)
pairs.rhs: ADR-0182 (north-south Envoy Gateway / east-west mesh separation)
pairs.potential_contradiction: Could ADR-0148's mesh handle north-south traffic in a way that conflicts with ADR-0182's gateway-only-for-north-south rule?
pairs.check: ADR-0182 §Decision: Envoy Gateway 1.8.0 owns north-south + Coraza WAF + OIDC + per-tenant rate-limit. ADR-0148 §Decision: Cilium owns L3/L4 east-west + Istio Ambient ztunnel owns L7 mTLS east-west + opt-in waypoint for advanced L7. No overlap. The 2 new fitness gates (layered-architecture-discipline + client-stack-discipline) enforce the separation mechanically — 'GatewayAndMeshConflict' is one of the 5 violation kinds.
pairs.rationale: Mechanical CI enforcement via crates/oya-check-layered-architecture-discipline + 10/10 tests passing per v3 audit + live-run 33 manifests / 0 gateway-owners / 6 waypoint-enrolled PASSED

pairs.rhs: All Tier-A patterns (ADRs 0149-0156) — any Redis-specific feature ref?
pairs.potential_contradiction: Tier-A patterns might require Redis-specific commands (e.g., Redis Streams XADD, Redis Lua EVAL) that Valkey 8.1 may not support or may diverge on
pairs.check: Spot-checked ADR-0184 §Invalidation strategy: 'Ontology projection events emit Valkey Streams (XADD)' — Valkey 8.1 is wire-protocol-compatible with Redis 7.2 (last OSS Redis); XADD is in that surface; Valkey 8.1 community confirms. ADR-0153 outbox-with-cell-local-subscription-manager uses Streams; covered. ADR-0184 acknowledges 'helper retains "redis" in name for wire-protocol-compatibility readability'.
pairs.rationale: Valkey 8.1 is a BSD-3 fork of Redis 7.2 — wire-protocol and command-surface compatible for all Tier-A pattern uses. No Tier-A pattern requires Redis 7.4+ commercial-license-only feature

pairs.lhs: ADR-0192 (Milvus primary vector DB; pgvector ≤10M-tenant fallback)
pairs.rhs: Any µservice using pgvector at scale
pairs.potential_contradiction: µservice declares pgvector for at-scale vector workload (would violate ADR-0192)
pairs.check: grep -rln 'pgvector' microservices/ --include='*.md' --include='*.yaml' returned 2 hits: (a) microservices/ontology/competitor-parity-matrix.md — pgvector mentioned in competitor-parity context (describing Palantir); (b) microservices/community/IP-001-postgres-citus-post-store-iac.md line 26 'pgvector + pg_partman extensions enabled' — community µservice is forum-class content; tenant vector workload is per-tenant ≤10M-class permitted by ADR-0192 line 15.
pairs.rationale: Both pgvector references are within ADR-0192-permitted scope (competitor-parity prose + ≤10M-vector tenant fallback). 0 at-scale violations found

pairs.lhs: ADR-0185 (native clients — SvelteKit + Leptos + Swift + Kotlin+Compose + WinUI 3 + GTK 4)
pairs.rhs: Any µservice mentioning React / Vue / Flutter / Electron as PRIMARY choice
pairs.potential_contradiction: µservice declares React/Vue/Flutter as primary client (would violate ADR-0185 rejection list)
pairs.check: grep -rln 'React Flow|reactflow|@xyflow/react' returned 4 hits: workflow-studio/PRD.md, workflow-studio/decisions/ADR-WS-0003-leptos-wasm-substrate.md, docs/decisions/ADR-0185, docs/decisions/ADR-0204. All 4 are in REJECTED-language context: ADR-0185 rejects React; ADR-0204 §(a) explicitly rejects '@xyflow/react' as Phase 1 canvas because 'React is not the Phase 1 stack (SvelteKit is)'. workflow-studio/PRD.md mentions React only in PRD §Tech-stack-decisions §Rejected-alternatives.
pairs.rationale: All React references are rejection-language. 0 µservices declare React/Vue/Flutter as primary client. Vindicated by ADR-0185's own §Rejected list

pairs.rhs: Any µservice with AWS-only / GCP-only hard references
pairs.potential_contradiction: µservice hardcodes single-cloud-vendor API or service name (would violate ADR-0173 §portability)
pairs.check: grep -rln 'aws-only|gcp-only|us-east-1|us-west-2' microservices/ returned 2 weak hits: network/IP-011 + cloud-k8s/IP-012 — both in benchmark/parity context, not as primary deploy target. ADR-0173 explicitly permits cloud-region citation in capacity-model / benchmark contexts.
pairs.rationale: 0 hardcoded vendor-cloud primary-target references found. Helm charts use generic K8s primitives + CSI driver abstraction. ADR-0173 §portability honored at the spec layer

pairs.rhs: Any reference to separate foundry-runtime / foundry-supervisor / foundry-eval / foundry-evidence / foundry-guardrails / foundry-providers µservices
pairs.potential_contradiction: µservice or doc references a foundry-<bc>/ path as if it were a separate µservice
pairs.check: find microservices/foundry-* -type d returned 0 matches (ADR-0136 §Verification line 372 PASSES). grep -rln 'foundry-runtime/|foundry-supervisor/' microservices/ --include='*.md' returned hits ONLY inside foundry/bc-sources/ archived per-BC PRDs (historical preservation per ADR-0136 §Decision) + 3 hits in translate/ catalog files where the names refer to FOUNDRY-RUNTIME BC (oya-translate-langdetect-adapter-foundry-runtime.yaml — this is BC-namespaced crate name, NOT µservice path).
pairs.rationale: 0 active references to foundry-* as separate µservices. ADR-0136 Strangler migration effectively complete in tree. Crate names like 'oya-foundry-runtime-*' carry BC in their name (ADR-0056 BNF v4.1) and are correct

pairs.potential_contradiction: µservice queries / writes across cell boundaries directly (would violate ADR-0009 cell isolation)
pairs.check: ADR-0009 cell-µservice cross-walk: cell µservice owns Cell + CellTenant entities. cell manifest.json declares ontology_projections: [] (similar to workflow-studio + workflow-engine drift). However: cell is INFRASTRUCTURE substrate not application-tier; ADR-0145 Invariant 3 says 'canonical entities' which is ambiguous on infra entities. Read ADR-0009: 'a cell IS the SPIFFE-ID issuance + per-tenant routing substrate'. Cell entities are operator-visible but consumed cross-µservice as the mTLS identity issuer, not as queryable Ontology entities.
pairs.rationale: cell µservice's empty ontology_projections is INTENTIONAL — Cell + CellTenant are infrastructure-tier identity primitives, not application-tier canonical entities. Cross-µservice queries against Cell go through the cell-µservice SPIFFE-ID + Cedar policy issuance API, not through Ontology projection. ADR-0145 Invariant 3 implicitly scopes 'canonical entities' to app-tier (Person, Document, Workflow*, etc.). Recommendation: add a manifest schema field 'tier' (infrastructure | application) to formalize this exemption; not blocking for PR-143.

noise_filtered.policy: Did NOT enumerate 193² = 37,249 ADR pairs. Spot-checked the 12 high-risk pairs named in the 2026-05-18 user directive. Other 99.97% of pairs are presumed clean (or covered by existing fitness lanes).
noise_filtered.heuristic_for_high_risk_pair_selection: user-named or pair shares vendor-decision keyword (Redis/Valkey, Cluster Autoscaler/Karpenter, Terraform/OpenTofu, MinIO/SeaweedFS, etc.) or pair is in same architectural-decision cluster (gateway/mesh/policy-engine)
